Silverstone (British GP) — survey report

Circuit id silverstone · UK · theme green, sceneryTheme permanent · day circuit (night:false) · branch cursor/silverstone-survey-a1 · base sha 680df66 · survey date 2026-10-15 · read-only (no js/css edits). Tooling merged: shared-shot-tooling-5b45 and day-wet-lighting-b7b8 (PR #1979), both clean with --no-ff.

Summary

  • Layout is faithful: 18 turns in the right order and direction (Abbey R, Farm L, Village R, Loop L, Aintree L, Brooklands L, Luffield R, Woodcote R, Copse R, Maggotts L, Becketts R-L-R, Chapel L, Stowe R, Vale L, Club R-R), built length 5846 m vs 5891 m real (-0.8 %).
  • verify-track OK, audit-circuit all six checks within baseline (float 0, clip 0, coplanar 7, buried 40).
  • Biggest visual problems: day sky stays clear blue (overcast, dry), storm looks like rain, orange autumn-coloured trees, a paddock hall hugging the Copse approach.
  • 63 of 69 planned frames captured (TLX, SwiftShader, 1280x720, downscaled).

Defects, ranked

#SevFinding and evidenceSuggested fix (not applied)
1HighDay sky ignores the authored British overcast: dry and overcast frames show a clear deep-blue sky with a crisp horizon.
def pal zenith [0.55,0.62,0.72] (js/circuits/silverstone.js:55) and scenery Object.assign(pal, ATM.britishOvercast) (scenery/silverstone.js:75) describe a pale grey-blue sky. Frames 01-06 (dry) and 58-63 (overcast) render saturated blue. Mechanism not traced; the sky gradient is probably driven by js/lighting/atmosphere.js (touched by the PR #1979 merge) rather than pal.		Trace which colour reaches the sky pass (lightState() or __apex.info()); make weather 'overcast' desaturate/lighten the day sky.
2MediumStorm is nearly identical to rain.
Compare frames 16-21 (rain) with 22-27 (storm): same grey grade and reflections, marginally heavier streaks.		Check the storm profile in js/race/weather-arc.js and the lighting blend; storm should darken further and thicken precipitation.
3MediumOrange/gold autumn-coloured crowns on a green summer circuit.
Visible in dry frames 02, 03, 05 and fog/overcast frames. The source colours are green: COPSE [0.12,0.36,0.16] (scenery/silverstone.js:80), oak() -> broadleafFall (:782-788; nature.js:725-749 uses the colour as given). The orange therefore comes downstream (MAT.FOLIAGE tint or the generic furniture.fol [0.28,0.45,0.22] in def line 77). Not traced further.		A/B with __apex.matTex(0); trace which species and tint produce orange.
4MediumPaddock hall 6 m from the road edge, 8 m high and 90 m long, hugs the Woodcote to Copse straight.
building(k(0.97),1,6,12,8,90,{kind:'hall'}) at scenery/silverstone.js:517. Legacy 0.97 + shift 0.5233 = racing 0.49, a live racing section; the comment calls it the old National-pit complex. Fills the foreground of orbit f50 frames (04, 19, 25, 49).		Move dist outward (>= 40 m) or drop it. The ten garage boxes at :761-773 (dist 6..132 at k(0.97)) share that anchor.
5MediumOrbit camera sits behind a huge pale, wood-grain-textured slab at the start line.
Orbit f00 frames 01, 16, 22, 46, 52, 58, 64. The slab has a plank-like texture, so a pale CONCRETE-material block is a candidate: BRDC clubhouse building(k(0.48),1,28,22,9,20,{kind:'chevron'}) at :439, or the Wing plinth (:459). Could not confirm which; the camera is the tool's orbit rig, so this is a framing defect as much as a prop one.		Identify the mesh (apex scene() hook near racing 0.0); check the baked texture mapping of MAT.CONCRETE on large faces.

Weather x time-of-day x lap-position gallery

Orbit camera at six lap fractions per condition (day dry also has EYE and trackside). Frame numbers match artifacts/shots/tracks/silverstone/. Files are named silverstone-NN-view-fPP-tod-weather.jpg.

Day · Dry 15 frames

Sky is a saturated clear blue with a hard horizon, not the pale British overcast the def authors (defect 1).

Day · Wet 6 frames

Sky greys and the road gets mirror reflections; vertical reflection streaks under trees. Response is correct.

Day · Rain 6 frames

Grey sky, dark saturation, streaks, reflections. Daytime no longer reads as night (PR #1979 merge applied).

Day · Storm 6 frames

Almost indistinguishable from rain: slightly heavier streaks only; no extra darkening or lightning (defect 2).

Day · Overcast 6 frames

Barely differs from dry: sky stays deep blue; only the horizon haze changes (defect 1).

Day · Fog 6 frames

Fog works: distance haze and pale far trees; sky above the haze stays clear blue.

Dusk · Dry 5 frames

Gold dusk grade, floodlight posts light pools on the verge. Lamps fire although the def is night:false.

Dusk · Rain 4 frames

Rain at dusk; wet reflections of lamp pools.

Night · Dry 3 frames

Lamp pools work; sky and horizon are pure black, far stands unlit.

Night · Rain 6 frames

Wet reflections of lamp pools; background near-black.

Not captured / uncertain

  • 6 frames failed (soft-present timeout after 3 retries): #28 dusk dry f00, #34-36 night dry f00/f17/f33, #40-41 dusk rain f00/f17. Not re-run: capture exceeded the ~60 min budget.
  • Not captured: eye or trackside in any weather other than dry day; dawn; storm at dusk or night; lap fractions between the six.
  • No numeric probes of the sky or foliage tint (defects 1 and 3 are visual with mechanism not traced); the f00 slab (defect 5) is unidentified.
  • Real-world elevation is uncertain (sources disagree); built 14 m range is compared only with the def brief.
  • Software renderer (SwiftShader), TLX backend: frames say nothing about a player's GPU.
